einzeiler: Labor market resilience clashes with stagnant wages and surging international travel.
kurzfassung: August jobs data revealed stronger-than-expected growth alongside a sharp slowdown in annual wage increases. Meanwhile, long-term bond yields climbed and American spending on international travel reached historic highs. The episode also explores how farmers and nontraditional students are adapting to mounting financial pressures.
stichpunkte: August employment numbers surpassed expectations with 162,000 new jobs added and the unemployment rate holding at 4.1%.
Average hourly earnings grew by 3.1% year-over-year, marking the slowest pace in over five years.
Long-term bond yields hit record highs, driven by differing views on government fiscal responsibility and AI-driven growth.
Farm equipment sales dropped more than 20% as producers rely on older machinery and DIY repairs to cut costs.
Americans made 6 million more trips to Europe in 2025 than in 2019, prioritizing experiential travel despite inflation.
The U.S. trade deficit expanded to its largest gap in 16 months, driven by increased shipments of technology hardware.

clips.hook: Markets expect the Fed to raise interest rates
clips.text: Financial markets reacted to the positive employment data by anticipating that central bankers will feel confident enough to increase borrowing costs.

clips.hook: Wage growth hits a five-year low
clips.text: Despite a robust employment report, annual hourly earnings increases fell to their lowest level in more than half a decade while consumer prices continued climbing.
Data from the Association of Equipment Manufacturers shows a steep double-digit decline in machinery purchases as agricultural producers tighten their budgets.

clips.hook: How American tourists outspend European locals
clips.text: Travel industry data reveals that U.S. visitors spend significantly more per day than their European counterparts and continue the custom of tipping service workers.

clips.hook: It is never too late to start studying
clips.text: A mother of six pursuing her degree reflects on the encouragement she received regarding her age and the time it takes to finish school.

beschreibung:
This economy added twice the amount of jobs expected in August, which is good news for the labor market. Still, the latest jobs report showed average hourly earnings were up just 3.1% annually — the slowest growth in more than five years. In this episode, when we can expect wages to start keeping up with inflation. Plus: American tourism to Europe is up, some farmers rely on decades-old machinery as budgets tighten, and one mom goes back to school 15 years after she started.
